records.label: 6-year-old girl
quotes: We report a 6 year old girl with an isolated humoral immune deficiency and a unique combination of dysmorphic features.

Physical findings include microcephaly, micrognathia, sickle shaped eyebrows, hypoplastic alae nasi, thenar hypoplasia, partial 4-5 syndactyly of toes, recessed great toes, anterior anus, and hypoplastic labia minora.
Laboratory evaluation revealed hypogammaglobulinaemia, absent B cells, and a 46,XX karyotype.

records.previously_reported: previously described by the authors as two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency (Hoffman syndrome)
quotes: We previously reported two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology (Table 1, Supplementary Table 1),. The probands from each family presented with recurrent infections by polysaccharide-encapsulated bacteria, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and absent CD19+ B cells, but had normal T-cell responses to mitogens.

One gene, TOP2B, which encodes topoisomerase IIβ, was affected by a heterozygous variant in each family: a de novo in-frame deletion c.1761_1763delAGA, p.EE587E, and a missense mutation c.1448C > T, p.S483L.

Hoffman syndrome patients have no detectable B cells in the peripheral blood, nor form germinal centers, and patients did not generate protective serologic titers to immunization; however, detectable amounts of circulating immunoglobulins indicate that some B cells are present, but are below the clinical limits of detection.

records.label: Family 3 patient

phenotypes.text: initially diagnosed as atypical Ablepharon-Macrostomia syndrome

variants.as_reported: a heterozygous TOP2B variant: c.1897G > A, p.G633S

quotes: A third patient initially being reported as having an atypical presentation of Ablepharon-Macrostomia syndrome, was later found to have humoral immunodeficiency. Independent reanalysis of clinical whole-exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous TOP2B variant: c.1897G > A, p.G633S.
Patients have normal numbers of CD4 and CD8 T cells, but no detectable peripheral B cells in blood (Table 1), despite cells originating from a common lymphocyte precursor.

notes.statement: Erdős et al. (2021) reported an inherited TOP2B mutation. They suggested that it may confirm mutational hotspots in the TOPRIM domain of TOP2B.
quotes: Inherited TOP2B Mutation: Possible Confirmation of Mutational Hotspots in the TOPRIM Domain.

notes.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) found that recombinant TOP2B A485P had more than 10-fold reduced DNA relaxation and decatenation activity. Coexpression with wildtype TOP2B lowered decatenation activity, which suggested a dominant-negative effect on wildtype TOP2B and TOP2A rather than haploinsufficiency.
quotes: We found that enzymatic activities of TOP2BA485P were reduced more than 10 fold

These results indicate that mutant TOP2BA485P protein not only itself has reduced intrinsic enzymatic activity, but also exerts a dominant negative effect on the activities of wild-type TOP2B and TOP2A.

notes.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) found reduced amounts of TOP2B protein in patient T cells, fibroblasts, and iPSCs. In HEK-293 cells, the mutant protein produced a degradation product, which suggested that it was less stable; it still interacted with TOP2A.
quotes: found reduced amounts of the TOP2B protein in patients’ cells in comparison to cells of healthy controls (Figure 2A)
We found a low molecular weight product of TOP2BA485P degradation, suggesting that the mutant protein is less stable than wild-type TOP2B

notes.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) found a complete absence of CD19+ cells in a patient's bone marrow, which indicated a block in B-cell development after the common lymphoid progenitor stage. They noted that the block is leaky, because some patients have immunoglobulins and small numbers of B cells.
quotes: This finding for the first time shows that TOP2B is critical during the earliest stages of B cell lineage after the Common Lymphoid Progenitor (CLP) stage (Figure 2H).
Nevertheless, in TOP2B deficiency this block is leaky, because immunoglobulins and small numbers of B cells have been found in peripheral blood of several patients

notes.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) concluded that BILU syndrome and Hoffman syndrome are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.
quotes: Our results indicate that BILU and Hoffman syndromes are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.

notes.statement: Papapietro et al. (2020) noted that the A485P mutation was absent from more than 90,000 subjects in gnomAD. In contrast, 42 unaffected gnomAD subjects carried heterozygous loss-of-function TOP2B variants, which argued against haploinsufficiency as the mechanism.
quotes: absent from more than 90,000 subjects in the gnomAD database
the gnomAD database has 42 such unaffected subjects

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) noted that the syndrome, previously described in two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology and subsequently named Hoffman syndrome, is characterized by agammaglobulinemia or hypogammaglobulinemia together with facial dysmorphism and limb anomalies.
quotes: We previously described two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology,. While agammaglobulinemia and hypogammaglobulinemia are common to several classic immunodeficiencies, the patients were also affected by facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies, identifying this as a unique syndrome, subsequently named Hoffman syndrome, but the genetic etiology remained unknown until now.

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) reported that Hoffman syndrome patients had no detectable B cells in peripheral blood and did not form germinal centers or generate protective serologic titers to immunization, although detectable circulating immunoglobulins indicated that some B cells were present below clinical limits of detection; CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell numbers and T-cell mitogen responses were normal, and NK cells were reduced in two of the patients.
quotes: Hoffman syndrome patients have no detectable B cells in the peripheral blood, nor form germinal centers, and patients did not generate protective serologic titers to immunization; however, detectable amounts of circulating immunoglobulins indicate that some B cells are present, but are below the clinical limits of detection. In contrast, patients show normal numbers of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes and T-cell mitogen stimulation.
The reduced numbers of NK cells in two of the patients (Table 1) may be consequent to similar binding patterns of Top2b to the Nfil3 promoter, a regulator of NK cell differentiation–.

notes.statement: In three families with Hoffman syndrome, Broderick et al. (2019) identified three heterozygous mutations in TOP2B (p.S483L, p.EE587E, and p.G633S), all affecting the TOPRIM (DNA gating) domain; they noted that TOP2B has a probability of loss of function intolerance (pLI) of 1, suggesting disease through haploinsufficiency or partial genetic dominance, and confirmed all mutations by Sanger sequencing.
quotes: All of the mutations affected the TOPRIM domain of TOP2B (Fig. 1b). Notably, TOP2B has a probability of loss of function intolerance (pLI) of 1 (Supplementary Table 5), similar to most known severe haploinsufficiency human disease genes, suggesting that the identified heterozygous mutations in our patients could cause disease either through haploinsufficiency or a partial genetic dominance.
In three families with Hoffman syndrome,, we identified three heterozygous mutations affecting the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of the type II topoisomerase TOP2B.
For all three families, mutations in TOP2B were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

notes.statement: Using Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Broderick et al. (2019) showed that chimeric or yeast TOP2 constructs carrying the patient mutations S483L, EE587E, or G633S failed to complement the temperature-sensitive top2-4 allele and did not support recovery of top2-delta haploid spore clones, indicating loss of topoisomerase II function; haploid strains heterozygous for the mutations grew more slowly and their nuclear fractions decatenated kinetoplast DNA less effectively than wild-type, indicating a partial dominant negative phenotype.
quotes: Similar to the mutant chimeric constructs but unlike the wild-type ScTOP2 plasmid, the mutant ScTOP2-S483L, -EE587E, and -G633S vectors were unable to complement the top2–4 at the nonpermissive temperature, consistent with a loss of function (Fig. 2a).

No haploid spore clones lacking TOP2 were recovered with an empty vector control or with the ScTOP2-EE587E, -S483L, or -G633S vectors (Fig. 2b). Taken together, these results indicate that each of our patient mutations disrupt topoisomerase II function.
Thus, the disease-associated versions of TOP2 have a partial dominant negative phenotype in S. cerevisiae based on growth and/or decatenation assays.

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) found that B cell-specific deletion of Top2b in mice (Top2b-/- mb1-cre and Top2b-/- cd19-cre) reduced peripheral CD19+ B cells, altered splenic follicle architecture, and reduced PrePro B, Pre B, and immature B cells in bone marrow and B cells at every splenic developmental stage, with reduced kappa-deleting recombination excision circles and reduced Pax5 but unchanged Rag1 expression; Top2b-/- mice did not survive the perinatal period.
quotes: To test the role of TOP2B in B-cell development, we bred Top2bflox2 mice to two independent B cell-specific cre mice: cd19-cre and mb1-cre, as Top2b−/− mice do not survive the perinatal period. Flow cytometry of peripheral blood demonstrated that Top2b−/−mb1-cre and Top2b−/−cd19-cre mice had fewer CD19+ B cells than wild-type controls (Fig. 3a, Supplementary Fig. 5a).

Immunophenotyping demonstrated that the bone marrow of Top2b−/−mb1-cre mice have fewer PrePro B cells, Pre B, and immature B cells compared to control mice (Fig. 3K). In the spleen, there were fewer B cells at every developmental stage compared to control mice (Fig. 3l).

Furthermore, expression of Pax5, a B-cell specific transcription factor expressed at most stages of B-cell development–, was significantly reduced in B cells derived from Top2b−/−mb1-cre mice while Rag1 expression was unchanged (Fig. 3n, o).

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) generated knockin mice carrying the murine equivalent of the patient TOP2B EE587E mutation; homozygotes were not viable, whereas Top2b+/EE587E heterozygotes had reduced spleen-to-body ratio, reduced total serum IgG, impaired antigen-specific antibody responses to ovalbumin and Pneumovax-23, reduced B cells at most developmental stages, reduced Pax5 and Foxo1 expression, and increased DNA strand breaks in B cells, with peripheral B cells reduced even compared with Top2b+/- mice while T cells were unaffected.
quotes: Top2bEE587E/EE587E homozygous mice were not viable, similar to Top2b−/− mice, but Top2b+/EE587E heterozygotes could be recovered, which mirror the genotype of the Hoffman syndrome patients (Supplementary Table 7).
Similar to patient proband A, Top2b+/EE587E mice had decreased peripheral blood B cells, which were reduced even compared to Top2b+/− mice, without an effect on peripheral blood T cells (Fig. 6a, b).

Splenic B cells isolated from Top2b+/EE587E mice had increased DNA breaks compared to B cells from Top2b−/− mb1 cre and wild-type mice as measured by the increase in comet tail length (Fig. 6e, f), while the comet tail length was not altered in T cells derived from Top2b mutants (Fig. 6g).

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) showed that B cells from Top2b+/EE587E mice secreted less total IgG, IgG3, and IgG2b after LPS stimulation with or without IL-4 and more than 90% failed to advance beyond the first division, while isolated splenic T cells produced normal amounts of IL-2 in response to PMA and ionomycin and proliferated normally, consistent with the normal T-cell mitogen responses seen in the patients.
quotes: In response to in vitro stimulation with LPS with or without IL-4, Top2b+/EE587E derived B cells demonstrated decreased secretion of total IgG, IgG3, and IgG2b compared to littermate controls (Fig. 7a, Supplementary Fig. 7a, b). In contrast, in vitro stimulation of isolated splenic T cells showed similar IL-2 production in response to PMA and ionomycin in both Top2b+/EE587E mice and controls (Fig. 7b).

After 5 days in culture, the majority of viable wild-type B cells had undergone 3–4 rounds of division, while more than 90% of mutant B cells did not advance beyond the first division (Fig. 7c, Supplementary Fig 7d.)

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) found that Top2b mRNA and protein were more highly expressed in wild-type murine B cells than in T cells, and proposed that the B cell-restricted phenotype reflects the preferential reduction of long gene transcription when topoisomerase function is lost, noting that murine B-cell transcription factor genes (EBF 390 kb, Pax5 178 kb, Foxo1 85 kb) are notably longer than T-cell (Tcf1 30 kb, Notch1 45 kb) or shared (Rag1 11 kb, E2A 24 kb) transcription factor genes.
quotes: B cells have greater expression of Top2b mRNA and protein compared to T cells (Fig. 6h, i), which is consistent with previous reports in both humans and mice–. Together these results suggest that Top2b is more active in B cells than in T cells.

One possible explanation for this specificity is that long gene transcription is preferentially reduced when topoisomerases are absent or inhibited,, and that the murine B-cell transcription factors are notably longer (EBF is 390 kb, Pax5 is 178 kb, and Foxo1 is 85 kb) compared to T-cell transcription factors (Tcf1 is 30 kb and Notch1 is 45 kb) or shared transcription factors (Rag1 is 11 kb and E2A is 24 kb).

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) reported that analysis of published Top2b ChIP-seq data and etoposide-induced END-seq breaks from murine primary B cells showed Top2b, but not Top2a, at the promoter and enhancer (intron 5) regions of Pax5, suggesting that defective Top2b activity could impair germline transcriptional activity and Igh locus accessibility, with negative effects on V(D)J recombination.
quotes: Analysis of published Top2b ChIP-seq data and etoposide-induced DNA breaks as determined by END-seq from murine primary B cells showed the presence of Top2b (but not Top2a) in the promoter and enhancer (intron 5) regions of Pax5 (Supplementary Fig. 8).
Impairments in germline transcriptional activity, caused by defective Top2b activity could affect Igh locus accessibility, with negative effects on V(D)J recombination.

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) noted that a brief clinical report had described a patient with progressive microcephaly, developmental delay, and hypotonia carrying a TOP2B variant outside the TOPRIM domain (H58Y), but that no similarities to their patients were identified and it was unclear whether that variant is causative.
quotes: Consistent with this latter possibility, a brief clinical report recently described a patient with progressive microcephaly, developmental delay, and hypotonia, who had a variant outside of the TOPRIM domain of TOP2B (H58Y). However, no similarities to our patients were identified and it is currently unclear if this variant is causative.

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) commented that a bone marrow biopsy had not been clinically indicated in their patients, leaving open where in B-cell development the failure occurs in humans, although their murine data suggested a reduced bone marrow B-cell compartment with surviving cells having reduced ability to respond to antigen or general stimuli.
quotes: A bone marrow biopsy has not been clinically indicated for patients, leaving open the question of where in B-cell development the failure occurs in humans; however, the analysis of the Top2b mutant mice suggests that in the absence of functional TOP2B, the bone marrow generates a reduced B cell compartment and that the remaining surviving cells have reduced ability to respond to antigen or general stimuli.

notes.statement: Broderick et al. (2019) noted that malignancy had not been observed in their patients or mice, despite the expectation that defects in forming or repairing DNA double strand breaks during immunoglobulin gene rearrangement might confer a greater tendency to malignancy.
quotes: While these recombination defects can lead to immunodeficiency,, we might expect a greater tendency to malignancy, which has not been observed in our patients or mice.

notes.statement: Kallish et al. (2011) noted that fewer than 20 patients with ablepharon-macrostomia syndrome had been reported. These included a parent with 2 children and a father with a daughter, which suggested autosomal dominant inheritance.
quotes: Fewer than 20 patients have been reported to date. These include a parent and two children and a recent report of a father and daughter, therefore suggesting autosomal dominant inheritance.

notes.statement: Hügle et al. (2011) concluded that their mother-daughter pair and the previously reported sporadic girl with humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies all represented the same condition, Hoffman syndrome, and reviewed the features of these 3 affected individuals.
quotes: One such report was a sporadic case of humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies in a young girl, later referred to as Hoffman syndrome.
We believe that all three cases described above represent the same condition.

notes.statement: In affected individuals from 2 families with BILU syndrome, Tischkowitz et al. (2004) found no mutation in the candidate gene HOXA13 by sequence analysis and no evidence of a microdeletion involving HOXA13 or the HOXA cluster as a whole.
quotes: In affected individuals from both families, sequence analysis of candidate gene HOXA13 did not identify a mutation, and there was no evidence of a microdeletion involving either HOXA13 or the HOXA cluster as a whole.

notes.statement: Tischkowitz et al. (2004) reported a second family with BILU syndrome showing autosomal dominant inheritance, and suggested that the association was a true syndrome.
quotes: Here, we report a second family with similar features, which also shows autosomal dominant inheritance.
add weight to the observation that this is a true syndromic association

notes.statement: Tischkowitz et al. (2004) further described the phenotype of BILU syndrome in females.
quotes: We further delineate the phenotype of this condition in females

notes.statement: Edery et al. (2001) suggested that the combination of B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities, and urogenital malformations in a 3-generation family might represent a novel autosomal dominant syndrome.
quotes: B cell immunodeficiency, distal limb abnormalities, and urogenital malformations in a three generation family: a novel autosomal dominant syndrome?

notes.statement: Hoffman et al. (2001) found that the patient's development was substantially slower than that of her twin. A review of the literature and the London Dysmorphology Database identified no recognizable syndrome matching her findings, and the authors suggested that she might represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology.
quotes: She has postnatal growth retardation and her development is substantially slower than her twin's.

A review of the literature and the London Dysmorphology Database did not produce any recognizable syndromes that match her constellation of findings. She may represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology.
